messages:
samir: Accepted the invite to the Acme org a few mins ago but all action buttons (Edit, Invite, Billing) are grayed out in Console. Clicking shows 403. Can someone check? :thinking:

maya_support: Sorry about that — can you paste repro steps and your org/project id? Also which SSO provider (Okta/Google/etc)?

samir: Steps: 1) Click accept invite link from email 2) landed in console at /orgs/acme/projects 3) top-right shows my name, but buttons are disabled 4) clicking Edit yields popup '403 permission denied'. Org ID: org-9a2b Project: prj-17. SSO: Okta SAML.

maya_support: Thanks. Can you try opening an incognito window and re-login? Also give us the session cookie and id_token (redact) if possible.

samir: Tried incognito and same. Sharing redacted id_token via DM. Here is the browser console when clicking Edit:

fetch("https://api.redwood.ai/projects/prj-17/edit", {headers:{Authorization: 'Bearer <id_token>'}})
=> 403 {"error":"forbidden","code":403,"detail":"insufficient_scope"}

Response header: x-auth-source: sso-okta

maya_support: Hmm 'insufficient_scope' — sounds like token scopes didn't include project:write. @ashwin_eng can you check auth logs and recent client rotations?

auth-bot: oauth-client client-789 rotated at 4532070000. Removed legacy scope mapping: on_behalf_of -> project:write. TraceID: tx-88f.

ashwin_eng: I see a rotation for the org's oauth client. The new client registration missed the OBO mapping that maps SAML groups -> RBAC scopes. That would cause id_tokens to lack project:write even if user is in Admin group. Escalating to idp team to re-add mapping.

karen_idp: Ack. We pushed a change during config sync: accidentally omitted the 'roles.claims' mapping for acme. I'll reapply the mapping and re-trigger SCIM sync. ETA ~20m.

devin_sre: As a temporary workaround, you (samir) can run a token refresh to get a new access token with scopes. In console devtools run:

POST https://auth.redwood.ai/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange",
  "subject_token": "<id_token>",
  "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token",
  "scope": "openid profile project:write"
}

If the exchange succeeds you'll get an access_token with project:write and Edit should work. If it still 403, stop and we will force a mapping apply.

maya_support: I'll keep monitoring. @karen_idp let us know when mapping is applied, we'll ask samir to re-login and verify.

auth-bot: Mapping applied for org-9a2b by karen_idp at 4532102000. SCIM sync triggered.

samir: Re-logged, still seeing gray buttons. Did a token exchange per Devin's snippet; got access_token but Edit still 403. Response detail now: 'role_unassigned'

ashwin_eng: Checking RBAC — looks like users were provisioned but group->role binding didn't provision due to SCIM partial failure during the sync window. We have a remediation script to reconcile group memberships. Running now.

auth-bot: RBAC reconcile job started for org-9a2b at 4532109000, job-id job-345.

ashwin_eng: Reconcile finished. Can you try again, samir?

samir: OK re-logged and buttons are active now. Edit works. Thanks everyone! :tada:

maya_support: Great — root cause: oauth client rotation removed role claim mapping + SCIM partial sync caused group->role binding omission. Action items: idp team to add validation in client rotation playbook, SRE to add post-rotation checks for role claims, support to notify acme about possible downtime window. I'll open a ticket.

maya_support: Closing thread after follow-up ticket: TKT-2026-89. Participants informed.
